title: Emerging roles of NV-diamond magnetometry in brain mapping and bioimaging
summary: Review of NV-diamond magnetometry for brain mapping. Records best sensitivity of 9.4 ± 0.1 pT/sqrt(Hz) at 5-100 Hz without flux concentrator (Tokyo Tech 2024). Notes superiority for nanoscale spatial resolution vs SQUID/OPM for single-neuron imaging. Addresses ambient-condition MEG candidacy: current state still pT-class, not fT-class for whole-brain MEG.

key_numbers.target_for_MEG: 1-10 fT/sqrt(Hz) (not yet achieved at room temperature)

bci_relevance: NV-diamond is a WATCH for BCI sensing: excellent for single-neuron/peripheral nerve, not yet viable for whole-brain MEG. Gap to fT is 4 orders of magnitude in noise power.
independent_researcher_budget: Single-channel demos possible ~$15k-20k but at pT level only. Suitable for magnetomyography / magnetoneurography, not MEG.
